## Analysis Summary

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean leaf (upper surface), green background
- Small, discrete dark reddish-brown spots scattered across the leaf
- Clear yellow/orange halos surrounding each dark lesion
- No vein-following pattern
- Some leaf holes (possibly insect damage or fallen-out lesion centers)

**Reference comparison conclusions:**
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Best match — small angular reddish-brown lesions with prominent yellow halos on upper surface; "centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered" matches the holes visible
- **Bacterial_Pustule**: Closer to pale green specks with greenish-yellow halos + pustule on underside — less matching
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Reference shows heavily yellowed/browning leaves, more advanced defoliation — not matching
- **Soybean_rust**: Pustules mainly on lower leaf surface — not matching
- **Cercospora**: Large purple patches, leathery — not matching
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Gray centers with reddish-brown margins, more circular — not matching
- **Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus**: Vein-following necrosis — not matching
- All others clearly eliminated

The prominent yellow halos surrounding dark reddish-brown lesions on the upper leaf surface, combined with what appears to be tattered leaf holes where lesion centers have fallen out, strongly points to **Bacterial_Blight**.
